Attachment C
Term Sheet for Cost Recovery of Power Up Projects
 Power Up New England Term Sheet
November 13, 2024

 Mechanism for Cost      Cost allocation and recovery provisions will be set forth in a
 Recovery                new attachment to the ISO-NE OATT (e.g., Attachment R). This
                         will include load/billing determinant-related terms.

                         The project revenue requirement will be calculated utilizing the
                         Settled Formula Rate (ISO-NE OATT Attachment F) on a
                         proposed new worksheet/attachment using the existing gross
                         plant allocator model to assign costs to a separate wholesale
                         rate.



 State Support           The TOs will make all filings with FERC that are necessary and
                         appropriate to memorialize and implement this term sheet.
                         NESCOE will allow the TOs to represent that NESCOE supports
                         the TOs’ filings and NESCOE will file supportive comments at
                         FERC for each TO FERC filing. NESCOE’s comments at FERC
                         will report on the NESCOE vote approving this term sheet and
                         NESCOE will note a unanimous vote in favor if the vote is
                         unanimous.

                         NESCOE consents to the TOs including a copy of this term
                         sheet as part of any or all of the aforementioned FERC filings.

                         In addition, NESCOE staff will help facilitate the TOs’ request
                         that the lead applicant of Power Up (namely, the
                         Massachusetts Department of Energy Resources) provide a
                         letter of support for the TOs’ FERC filings that reflects that the
                         state agencies that signed on to the DOE application for Power
                         Up support the project. Subsequent to NESCOE and/or the
                         states making any of their initial communications with state
                         agencies regarding Power Up, NESCOE staff will also attend
                         meetings that the TOs request with state agencies and
                         NESCOE staff will express NESCOE’s support for Power Up at
                         these meetings.

 Abandonment/Cancelled   TOs will seek FERC approval for recovery of 100% of prudently
 Plant Costs             incurred project costs, inclusive of any development costs,
                         investment in cancelled plant, and ISO-NE deposits and/or
                         withdrawal penalties, if their respective project is cancelled,
                         terminated, or abandoned. Agreement on abandonment costs is
                         not conditional on DOE grant payments.

                                       1 of 5
 Cost Allocation   TOs will seek regional cost allocation as endorsed by the New
                  England states and will propose to spread the allocated revenue
                  requirements across all regional network load in New England on
                  a load ratio basis.

Recovery Period   Recovery period for capital investment will be based on the
                  useful life of transmission facilities, utilizing FERC-approved
                  depreciation rates per Appendix D to Attachment F. Expenses
                  shall be recovered for the duration that each TO’s project is in
                  service.

DOE Funding       DOE grant payments received by the TOs for their projects will
                  be treated as a credit against project costs, as reimbursed, net of
                  tax impact. Any remaining project costs will be recovered under
                  the new transmission wholesale rate using a new rate schedule
                  based upon OATT Attachment F as described above.
Base ROE          TOs will seek to apply the full FERC-approved New England ROE
                  (currently 11.07%). Any change in the approved New England
                  base ROE or incentive adders would result in a corresponding
                  change to the ROE allowed for Power Up.

Project Budget    The finalized project budget (the “Final Project Budget”),
Modifications     from which cost variances and the Cost Management
                  provisions discussed infra will be measured, shall be based
                  upon each TO’s estimated capital costs included in a report
                  to be provided by the TOs no later than three (3) months
                  after appeal deadlines for siting and permitting approval for
                  the TOs’ projects passes and after any appeals have been
                  finally adjudicated. The TOs shall provide said report
                  regardless of whether a report is otherwise due under the
                  annual reporting schedule described below (see Cost
                  Transparency, infra).

                  Each TO’s Final Project Budget may be modified after provision
                  of the report to account for cost changes that arise from: (1) the
                  DOE negotiating process; (2) Change in Laws, so long as a
                  change in law results in either (a) a delay of at least six months
                  or (b) an increase in project cost estimate of at least 10%, or (3)
                  Force Majeure. The TOs will present any of these
                  aforementioned Final Project Budget modifications and an
                  explanation for those proposed budget modifications to
                  NESCOE as soon as reasonably practicable, and, in any event,
                  before seeking to actualize them with any relevant regulatory
                  authority, if necessary.



                                2 of 5
 Cost Transparency
                    Commencing on Jan. 15, 2025, and annually no later than
                    Jan. 15 thereafter, and ceasing once each project is placed
                    in service, the TOs will provide a draft report to NESCOE that
                    will include each TO’s updated actual and projected project
                    costs (that TO’s “Actual Project Costs” and “Projected
                    Project Costs,” respectively) and a variance analysis of the
                    ongoing Actual Project Costs and Projected Project Costs
                    compared to each TO’s original estimate included in the
                    DOE grant application, or the Final Project Budget once
                    available, and as such may be modified in the Project Budget
                    Modifications section above, and will assess each TO’s
                    performance in containing project costs. The report shall
                    also include updated Excel files used in the GRIP budget with
                    DOE – the 3195-1855_DOER Budget Justification sheet.

                    The TOs shall provide to NESCOE any reports delivered to
                    the MA DOER DOE grant project manager, including any
                    updated Excel files used in the GRIP budget with DOE – the
                    3195-1855_DOER Budget Justification sheet, within 15 days
                    of issuance of such reports or files.

                    The TOs will provide funding for NESCOE to hire a consultant
                    to review the contents of each annual report and will
                    respond to questions from NESCOE regarding the contents
                    of the report in a manner (form and timing) similar to the
                    Attachment F Protocols. All TO costs associated with this
                    effort shall be recoverable as an expense.

                    Commencing on May 15, 2025, and annually no later than
                    May 15 thereafter, the TOs will provide to the ISO New
                    England Planning Advisory Committee (“PAC”) a final copy
                    of the report, any questions received from NESCOE, and any
                    responses, except that questions and answers containing
                    confidential business information will not be shared.

                    For avoidance of doubt, the term “Actual Project Costs”
                    shall include any and all costs funded by the DOE grant. The
                    Actual Project Costs less any and all costs funded by the DOE
                    grant shall be referred to as the “Actual TO Contribution.”
                    The Actual Project Costs and Actual TO Contribution
                    identified in the report shall be the inputs used in the Cost
                    Management section, infra.




                                  3 of 5
 Community Benefit Plans    Community benefit plan costs that are identified in the Power
                           Up DOE Community Benefits application will be recovered
                           without ROE.

Project Termination       If a TO’s Projected Project Costs are projected to exceed the TO’s
                          original estimate included in the DOE grant application (for
                          clarity $218,706,435 for Eversource and $369,866,344, which
                          included contingency, for NGRID) at certain points in time,
                          NESCOE shall have the right to terminate the project developed
                          by that TO, subject to that TO fully recovering all costs prudently
                          incurred prior to termination. The certain points in time at which
                          the termination right shall accrue are at the time of and any time
                          within three months after any of the following: (1) the end of the
                          annual reporting cycle (e.g., as described in the Cost
                          Transparency section; beginning January 15 and ending on May
                          15), (2) ISO study completion, (3) siting and permitting approval,
                          (4) the provision to NESCOE of any reports delivered to the MA
                          DOER DOE grant project manager, and (5) proposed cost
                          modifications as outlined in the Project Budget Modifications
                          section. Termination rights for each TO project will expire once
                          that project is placed into service.




                                         4 of 5
 Cost Management            Each TO will be allowed to earn an ROE of 11.07% (subject
                           to adjustments if the New England base ROE or incentive
                           adders change, as described in Base ROE above) on its
                           Actual TO Contribution, up to an amount equal to the Initial
                           Over-ride Dead Band. The Initial Over-ride Dead Band shall
                           be calculated by multiplying the Final Project Budget by
                           1.05 (i.e., increased by 5%). A second incremental band
                           shall be calculated by adding 15% of the Final Project
                           Budget to the Initial Over-ride Dead Band. Six additional
                           incremental bands shall be calculated by adding 10% of the
                           Final Project Budget to each preceding incremental band.

                           To control costs, if a TO’s Actual Project Costs exceed its
                           Initial Over-ride Dead Band, the ROE for that increment of
                           cost exceedance will be reduced by 65 basis points. The
                           ROE will continue to be reduced by 65 basis points for each
                           incremental 10% cost overrun (herein an “Incremental
                           Band”). This further reduction of ROE will only be applied
                           to the increment of cost within that Incremental Band.

                           In addition, if a TO’s Actual Project Costs are less than the
                           Final Project Budget, that TO will be allowed to earn a total
                           return amount that is equivalent to the return amount that
                           TO would have been entitled to if the Actual Project costs
                           had been equal to the Final Project Budget.

Billing                    NESCOE, the New England States, and the TOs will coordinate
                           and collaborate to seek commitment from ISO-NE to act as
                           billing agent for multistate cost allocation using regional
                           network load.
Future Capital Additions   Future capital additions will be added to rate base as projects
                           are placed in-service and recovered over the depreciable life of
                           the capital additions in accordance with FERC-approved
                           depreciation rates in Appendix D to Attachment F.

Uniqueness of Project      This proposal is provided in the context of the unique nature of
                           this project, including but not limited to the impact of DOE
                           funding on the project’s profitability, and should not be
                           considered precedent for future projects.




                                         5 of 5
